source.description: Project ByteStream load point that reads attacker-controlled bytes from the PoC-backed DataBuffer; callers consume the returned integers as PhaseOne strip metadata.

sink.description: MSan crash location reached while checking whether an output image row was fully initialized.

root_cause.description: The constructor only checks that the strip count equals image height, but does not validate that strip row numbers cover every row exactly once and are in range.

taint_source.description: Reads typed values from the attacker-controlled ByteStream; the return value is consumed by the fuzz target as strip count, row number, and strip length.

tainted_value_origin.description: A concrete attacker-controlled strip row index is materialized from the ByteStream and stored in each PhaseOneStrip.

root_cause_analysis.summary: The PoC controls PhaseOne strip metadata read from ByteStream, especially the strip row number `n`. The vulnerable constructor verifies only that the number of strips equals the image height, but it does not verify that row numbers are in range, unique, and collectively cover all image rows. A malformed strip list can therefore decompress one row more than once while leaving another allocated row untouched. The final initialization check reads every row and MSan reports the untouched row as use-of-uninitialized-value.
root_cause_analysis.why_patch_works: The patch adds validateStrips(), called from the constructor. It builds a histogram of strip row numbers, rejects out-of-bounds rows, rejects duplicates, and requires one strip per row. That prevents malformed strip metadata from skipping an output row, so every allocated row is decompressed before checkMemIsInitialized reads it.
